text:
Clara: quick sync on golden rotation + compatibility shim idea after last RFC. want to avoid flapping perf signals from stale samples.
Dmitri: yeah, we've seen benches regress when golden inputs age or when tokenizer tweaks change tokenization. what are you thinking?
Clara: two parts: 1) rotate golden sample subset on a schedule (rolling window) with traceable IDs, 2) compatibility shim layer to canonicalize tokenization differences for bench comparisons.
Hannah: hmm canonicalize how? tokenizers differ a lot (bpe merges, special tokens).
Clara: shim would be lightweight: normalize whitespace, map model-specific special-token encodings to a canonical sentinel, and record tokenization diff metrics. not trying to emulate tokenizers, just make bench diffs interpretable.
Dmitri: edgecases: if a model's tokenizer fundamentally changes (vocab swap), we should fail the fast gate and require a manual review. shim only for small drift/normalization.
QA-Bot: NOTE: proposal received. Fast-gate behavior: if tokenizer_hash changes -> block onboarding. If tokenization_diff_rate > 2% but no crash -> mark "token-drift-warn" and continue.
Hannah: rotation cadence? monthly feels coarse; maybe stratified: hot models rotate weekly (high traffic), cold models monthly. each rotation keeps overlapped seed-sets so we can do A/B comparisons.
Clara: yep. design: maintain seed-set table with fields: id, model_id, created_at, coverage_buckets (seqlen, unicode_class), origin (live/curated), status (active/retired), prev_id. Bench runner accepts seed_set_id and writes it into artifact metadata.
Dmitri: nice. how do we pick replacements? automated sampler that prefers under-covered seqlen buckets and recent heavy prefixes. keep size small (~250). curator can swap entries for edgecases.
Hannah: cost implications: rotating means more bench runs if we want to compare old vs new. I propose we only run full-comparison (old vs new) on a rotation event for hot models; otherwise just swap active.
Clara: good. and add a cheap delta-check job: after rotation, run a 10-min smoke comparing metric deltas. if delta > threshold, mark rotation as suspect and revert.
Dmitri: what's the threshold? maybe 5% p50 latency or 10% tokens/s? we should use multiple signals.
Clara: multi-signal rule: if >=2 signals exceed per-metric thresholds -> fail rotation. signals: p50 latency, p95 latency, tokens/s, quality regression (if evals exist).
Hannah: compatibility shim also needs to emit a token-diff artifact: for each seed, record token_count_model vs token_count_canonical and common prefix alignment. helps triage.
QA-Bot: ACTIONS: add fields to bench artifact: seed_set_id, rotation_id, token_diff_summary, rotation_passed=true/false. Add rotation smoke job to onboarding pipeline.
Dmitri: ownership: I'll implement seed-store and rotation job. Clara you want the shim and rotation policy?
Clara: yes, i'll spec the normalization rules and rotation config (cadence per traffic tier). Hannah pick the triage runbook for rotation failures?
Hannah: on it. runbook: auto-revert + create incident ticket if rotation fails on hot models; for cold models create a dev task.
Dmitri: one more: make sure rollout dashboards can filter by rotation_id so we don't mix pre/post-rotation metrics.
Clara: good catch. we'll add rotation_id tag to all perf dashboards and to the model registry UI.
OnboardBot: REMINDER: when opening PRs, include migration plan for existing seed-sets and a small data-cleanup script to mark old seed-sets as retired.
Hannah: timeline: 2 sprints for MVP (seed-store + minimal rotation smoke + shim prototype). aim to keep initial rollout opt-in for a subset of models.
Clara: thanks team 97 i'll open the RFC follow-up PR with schema changes and a short example of token_diff output.
Dmitri: :thumbsup:
Hannah: :rocket:
